newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to cut car tariffs to 10pct in 2005.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to cut car tariffs to 10pct in 2005.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, under pressure from business leaders and unions, said on Thursday that the government would cut car tarrifs to only 10 percent in the year 2005.
"From the first of January, the year 2000, the tariff will be 15 percent in accordance with existing legislative arrangements," Howard told reporters.
"It will remain at that level until the first of January 2005. We will legislate forthwith to reduce it on January 1, 2005, to 10 percent."
Howard said an export assistance scheme consistent with World Trade Organisation rules would to replace an existing scheme in 2000, and run until 2005.
Howard said there would be a further review of tariffs and assistance after 2005.
Car tariffs are due to fall to 15 percent by 2000, from 22.5 percent now, under arrangements already in place.
Howard warned the tariff cuts and industry assistance package would be dropped entirely if the upper house, the Senate, amended the measures.
The government's main industry advisory body, the Productivity Commission, had urged tariffs be cut to five percent by 2004.
Howard said the government remained committed to its obligations to cut trade barriers to zero by 2010 under the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum free trade pact.
"As far as APEC is concerned, we remain committed to the APEC goal," he said.
But he said the APEC target did not lay down specific strategies for specific industries.
